concepts.name: Nominal GDP: Definition and Measurement
key_dimensions: Measured using current year prices — susceptible to price-level changes
Does NOT reflect actual change in output volume — a classic UPSC trap
Can rise even when physical production falls (if prices rise sufficiently)
Used in debt-to-GDP ratio calculations — policy relevance

concepts.name: Real GDP: Definition and Measurement
key_dimensions: Measured using constant prices of a chosen base year — isolates volume change
Preferred metric for comparing economic growth across time periods
Can be lower than Nominal GDP in inflationary economies and higher in deflationary ones
India currently uses 2011-12 as the base year — frequently asked factual anchor

concepts.name: GDP Deflator: Construction and Interpretation
key_dimensions: Formula: (Nominal GDP / Real GDP) × 100 — must-know derivation
Measures economy-wide inflation unlike CPI or WPI which cover baskets
Includes all goods and services produced domestically — broader than CPI
A GDP Deflator > 100 indicates price level has risen above base year — directional logic trap

concepts.name: GDP Deflator vs CPI: Key Differences
key_dimensions: CPI uses a fixed consumer basket; GDP Deflator covers entire domestic output — scope difference
CPI includes imported goods; GDP Deflator excludes imports — critical UPSC trap
GDP Deflator automatically updates weights (Paasche index); CPI uses fixed weights (Laspeyres index)
RBI uses CPI for monetary policy, not GDP Deflator — institutional relevance

concepts.name: Base Year Selection and Revision
key_dimensions: Base year should represent a 'normal' economic year — criteria for selection
Base year revision can dramatically change GDP growth estimates — policy controversy
2015 MCA-21 data incorporation during 2011-12 base year revision — raised GDP estimates, created controversy

concepts.name: Price Index Types: Laspeyres vs Paasche vs Fisher
key_dimensions: Laspeyres uses base-year quantities as weights — tends to overestimate inflation (substitution bias)
Paasche uses current-year quantities — tends to underestimate inflation
Fisher Index is geometric mean of both — considered 'ideal' index
GDP Deflator is a Paasche-type index; CPI is a Laspeyres-type — comparison trap

concepts.name: Real GDP Growth Rate as Economic Welfare Indicator
key_dimensions: Real GDP growth ≠ improvement in welfare — ignores distribution, sustainability, non-market activities
Per capita Real GDP is a better comparator across countries/years than aggregate Real GDP
Limitations: excludes informal economy, unpaid household work, environmental degradation
Alternative indicators: HDI, GPI (Genuine Progress Indicator), Green GDP — UPSC loves alternatives

concepts.name: Relationship Between Nominal GDP, Real GDP, and Inflation
key_dimensions: Nominal GDP Growth ≈ Real GDP Growth + Inflation (GDP Deflator) — approximate identity
Distinguishing 'growth in output' vs 'growth in prices' — core analytical skill
Stagflation scenario: Nominal GDP may rise while Real GDP stagnates — policy trap
Deflation scenario: Real GDP > Nominal GDP — counterintuitive but examinable

concepts.name: Constant Price vs Current Price GDP in Indian Statistical Releases
key_dimensions: CSO/NSO releases GDP in both current and constant prices — institutional source
Advance Estimates, Revised Estimates, and Final Estimates sequence — process awareness
First Advance Estimate released in January (for budget preparation) — policy linkage
Differences between advance and final estimates — reasons for revision

concepts.name: Real GDP Per Capita: Cross-Country Comparisons and PPP Adjustment
key_dimensions: Nominal exchange rate conversion distorts cross-country Real GDP comparison
Purchasing Power Parity (PPP) adjustment accounts for price level differences across nations
India's GDP rank differs significantly in nominal USD terms vs PPP terms — factual trap
World Bank and IMF use PPP-adjusted figures for development comparisons — institutional context

concepts.name: GDP at Factor Cost vs GDP at Market Price: Interaction with Real/Nominal Distinction
key_dimensions: GDP at Market Price = GDP at Factor Cost + Indirect Taxes – Subsidies
India switched to GDP at Market Price as headline number in 2015 base year revision — key change
GVA (Gross Value Added) at basic prices replaced GDP at factor cost — terminology shift trap
Real vs Nominal distinction applies to both GVA and GDP — layered concept

concepts.name: Implicit Price Deflator vs Explicit Price Indices
key_dimensions: GDP Deflator is an 'implicit' deflator — derived, not directly measured
WPI and CPI are explicit/direct price indices with predefined baskets
Implicit deflator can diverge significantly from WPI/CPI during structural shifts
Sectoral deflators (agriculture, industry, services) used for sector-specific Real GVA — granular application

concepts.name: Nominal GDP and Fiscal/Debt Metrics
key_dimensions: Fiscal deficit as % of GDP uses Nominal GDP — denominator effect
Rising Nominal GDP can reduce debt-to-GDP ratio even without actual debt reduction — inflation dividend
FRBM targets are expressed as % of Nominal GDP — legislative relevance
Debt sustainability analysis requires distinguishing real interest rate from nominal — advanced application

concepts.name: Chain-Based vs Fixed-Base Real GDP Measurement
key_dimensions: Fixed-base method: single base year used throughout — simpler but distorts over long periods
Chain-linking: base year updated annually — reduces substitution bias, more accurate
USA uses chain-linked GDP; India uses fixed-base (2011-12) — comparative systems trap
Chain-linked Real GDP figures are not additive across components — a subtle but examinable trap

concepts.name: Sectoral Real GDP and Structural Transformation
key_dimensions: Differential deflators applied to Agriculture, Industry, and Services sectors
Structural shift: declining share of Agriculture in Real GDP vs relatively stable Nominal share when food inflation is high
Services sector deflator construction is methodologically complex — data limitation
Premature deterioralization debate — requires Real GDP sectoral data, not Nominal

concepts.name: Green GDP and Environmentally Adjusted National Accounts
key_dimensions: Green GDP = Conventional GDP – Cost of Environmental Degradation
Attempts to make Real GDP a true welfare measure by incorporating natural capital depletion
System of Environmental-Economic Accounting (SEEA) — UN framework, India's adoption status
India's GDP growth rate would be significantly lower if natural resource depletion were accounted for — policy implication

concepts.name: Nominal GDP Targeting as Monetary Policy Framework
key_dimensions: Alternative to inflation targeting — targets the sum of Real growth + Inflation
Advantage: automatically accommodates supply shocks without excessive tightening
Debate: India uses flexible inflation targeting (CPI-based), not Nominal GDP targeting
Nominal GDP targeting implies tolerance for higher inflation during recessions — policy trade-off trap

concepts.name: GDP Measurement Methods and Their Real vs Nominal Application
key_dimensions: Three methods: Expenditure, Income, and Value Added — all yield same Nominal GDP
Deflation to arrive at Real GDP applied differently: output method uses price indices by sector
Expenditure method deflation: separate deflators for consumption, investment, government spending, trade
Inconsistencies across methods in practice — a source of statistical discrepancy

concepts.name: GDP Growth Overestimation/Underestimation Controversies in India
key_dimensions: 2015 back-series controversy: new methodology showed higher GDP, questioned by economists
Arvind Subramanian's critique (2019): India's Real GDP growth overstated by ~2.5% post-2011
Informal sector deflation methodology questioned — wage data vs price data mismatch
Demonetization and GST impact on Real GDP measurement — informal economy capture failure

concepts.name: Real GDP and Business Cycle Analysis
key_dimensions: Business cycles defined in terms of Real GDP fluctuations, not Nominal — definitional anchor
Recession: two consecutive quarters of negative Real GDP growth (technical definition)
Output gap = Actual Real GDP – Potential Real GDP — used in fiscal and monetary policy calibration
India's use of 'advance estimates' vs 'revised estimates' creates lags in cycle identification
